title: Columbus's $500M Bond Gets Its First Project: 23 Permanently Affordable Condos on the East Side

body:
Columbus broke ground in late August on the Broad & Gould Condominiums — 23 for-sale homes on the East Side priced at roughly $199,000 each — the first visible deployment of the $500 million Affordable Housing Bond Columbus voters approved in November 2025.

The groundbreaking ceremony took place August 27 at the southeast corner of East Broad Street and South Gould Road, where a vacant lot will become a four-story building containing 23 two- and three-bedroom condominiums. Units range from 950 to 1,300 square feet. Completion is targeted for fall 2027.

## What 'permanently affordable' actually means here

The Broad & Gould project uses a community land trust structure, which is meaningfully different from how most affordable housing programs work.

In a conventional affordable housing deal — including many built with Low Income Housing Tax Credits — affordability restrictions expire after a set period, typically 15 to 30 years. After that clock runs out, units can be sold or rented at market rate. A community land trust prevents that outcome by severing ownership of the land from ownership of the building.

Under the [Central Ohio Community Land Trust](https://www.coclt.org/) model, COCLT retains ownership of the land beneath the Broad & Gould building in perpetuity. Buyers purchase their individual condominium units and hold a 99-year ground lease on the underlying land, paying a nominal monthly land lease fee rather than a land purchase price. When a homeowner sells, the resale price is calculated using a formula that limits appreciation and requires the next buyer to meet the same income qualifications. The home remains affordable through every subsequent transaction — not just the first.

## The bond funding

Columbus voters approved a [\$500 million Affordable Housing Bond](https://www.columbus.gov/Services/Housing-Assistance-Programs/Housing-Programs/Affordable-Housing-Bond-Investments) in November 2025 as part of a broader \$1.9 billion bond package. It is the largest local affordable housing commitment in Columbus history. Mayor Ginther's administration announced in early 2026 that the bond will fund four priority areas: preserving and building affordable rental units, upgrading the shelter system and transitional housing, land acquisition near major transit corridors, and innovation in construction methods and financing.

The Broad & Gould Condominiums draw on that fund through a \$10 million City Council allocation to COCLT for affordable homeownership development, [reported by 10TV](https://www.10tv.com/article/news/local/boomtown-ohio/columbus-city-council-approves-10-million-affordable-housing-central-ohio-community-land-trust/530-7fa7b531-8f4c-4218-9798-e540a5ef2bd7) when the Council approved it. Of that allocation, \$3 million is directed toward construction of the Broad & Gould project and an additional \$1.1 million is reserved for homebuyer assistance, according to [ABC6 On Your Side](https://abc6onyourside.com/news/local/home-affordability-crisis-continues-as-city-announces-199k-condos-coming-to-the-east-side).

Finance Fund, a Columbus-based community development financial institution, is a third partner. The organization has previously provided New Markets Tax Credit financing to other Columbus affordable housing and community development projects. Its specific financing instrument in the Broad & Gould deal has not been publicly detailed.

## Who qualifies — and what buyers get

To purchase a Broad & Gould condo, buyers must earn no more than 120 percent of the Columbus area median income and meet COCLT's homebuyer orientation requirements. For context, the Columbus HUD area median income for 2026 puts 120 percent at roughly \$86,000 for a single person and higher for larger households; the threshold is intended to serve working families who earn too much to qualify for rental subsidies but too little to purchase homes at market rates.

At \$199,000, the condos price far below the Columbus metro median sale price — the [July 2026 Columbus REALTORS report](https://columbusrealestatenews.com/blog/columbus-july-home-sales-climb-6-as-inventory-hits-decade-high) put the regional median at \$350,000, up 2.3 percent year-over-year — giving first-time buyers a real entry point into homeownership on the East Side rather than a rental subsidy that builds no equity.

## East Side context

The building will sit at the southeast corner of East Broad Street and South Gould Road. East Broad is one of Columbus's major east–west arterials, extending from downtown toward Bexley and beyond. The corridor east of the city center has seen scattered new investment over the past five years but no large-scale wave of market-rate condo development, which is partly why a \$199,000 for-sale price point is viable here in a way it would not be in Short North or German Village.

COCLT already operates an affordable homeownership portfolio across Columbus. An earlier project — Warner Junction in Franklinton — delivered units for first-time buyers below \$199,000 on lots on Rich Street and Grubb Street. The Broad & Gould project is larger in unit count and marks the trust's first ground-up new construction financed with the city's 2025 housing bond.

## What to watch next

The immediate milestone is construction progress through winter 2026 toward the fall 2027 completion. Once units are available, COCLT will run a homebuyer lottery or waitlist; the process and eligibility requirements will be posted at [coclt.org](https://www.coclt.org/).

Longer term, this project is the first public test of how the \$500 million bond performs at the neighborhood scale. Mayor Ginther has committed to quarterly reporting on bond deployment. If Broad & Gould delivers on schedule, the city and COCLT have a replicable template: vacant East Side lots, land trust ownership, city bond construction financing, and \$199,000 price points that connect to a market of buyers who have been priced out of the for-sale market without being eligible for rental subsidy programs.
